transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Cobalt Head of ML), Tom Rivers (CTO), Evan Liu (Data Engineer)

Summary:
Redwood demo of the Eval/Quality Monitoring feature set: prompt set management, regression alerts, A/B comparisons, integrations with Console and API + Redwood Optimize recommendations. Customer wants to validate alerting sensitivity, run comparative evals, and pilot with a 2-week eval account.

Topics:
- Prompt set versioning and storage
- Regression alerts and alerting policies (thresholds, cadence)
- A/B model comparisons and dashboards
- Integration with CI/CD and Slack/pager channels
- Data residency & SOC2/KMS questions

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Quick intros?
[00:12] Priya Singh: Yeah hi I'm Priya, Head of ML at Cobalt, focus on recommendations and NLU pipelines, we've been looking at drift and QA for our chat assistants.
[00:25] Tom Rivers: Tom here, CTO, interested in prod stability and compliance, I'll lurk mostly.
[00:32] Evan Liu: Evan, data engineer, I'll be doing the integration work.
[00:40] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood, I'll take the demo walkthrough, show Console and API flows, and the Optimize suggestions.
[00:48] Maya Chen: Quick agenda: show prompt-sets, run an A/B, show regression alerts firing on a synthetic regression, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:58] [01:05] Diego Alvarez: Ok opening the Console - apologies for my wifi, screen might lag a bit. So this is the Eval tab, we store prompt-sets as named artifacts; you can tag them with metadata like dataset, intent, steward. Example: "checkout_flow_q3".
[01:35] Priya Singh: Do you store the raw prompts or hashed versions? We can't send PII out of region.
[01:44] Nina Park: Good call. We support both: hashed-only ingest and encrypted prompt blobs via customer-managed KMS for Private. For hosted, you can opt into prompt-redaction and retention windows.
[02:05] Evan Liu: Is prompt hashing reversible?
[02:08] Nina Park: No, irreversible salted hash on our side unless you're on Private with customer keying and they keep plaintext locally.
[02:15] Tom Rivers: How about the eval runs, are these synchronous or batched? We do large sets nightly.
[02:22] Diego Alvarez: You can run eval jobs via API or Console. Batching is supported, and Redwood Optimize will suggest batching params to reduce token costs while meeting latency targets.
[02:33] [03:00] Diego Alvarez: Here's an A/B comparison we ran: Model A is a tuned open-quant model, Model B is a larger baseline. We compute metrics per prompt-set: exact-match, ROUGE-ish, and a custom human-similarity score. The dashboard shows deltas and confidence intervals.
[03:25] Priya Singh: That human-similarity score - is that based on embeddings?
[03:29] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we use a dense embedding similarity plus a learned calibration layer. Note - sounds like "human-similarity" but it's an automated proxy, you should still do spot check human evals.
[03:45] Evan Liu: Can we hook these results to our internal CI? Like fail a deploy if the QA score drops more than x?
[03:52] Diego Alvarez: Yep. We provide a CI API and a webhook push. You can set a regression alert policy: metric, window, threshold, and then we send alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or your webhook.
[04:10] [04:40] Priya Singh: I want to see an example of a regression alert - can you show a demo trigger?
[04:45] Diego Alvarez: Sure, will run a synthetic regression by swapping in a lower-quality model variant. Running job now...
[05:15] [05:45] Maya Chen: While that's running, quick note on prompt-sets: you can stage versions, pin a baseline, and tag failing prompts for manual curation which then feeds into model retrain or prompt rewrite workflows.
[06:05] [06:20] *(screen shows job run progress, a few network hiccups, some words transcribed as "Reedwood Opt" in the notes)*
[06:45] Diego Alvarez: Ok job finished - dashboard shows metric drop: overall QA score down 7.2% with a big hit on intent-recognition. Alert rule matched (threshold 5%). Sending alert now...
[07:05] [07:20] Priya Singh: I like seeing which prompts triggered the worst deltas, that's helpful. Can we annotate with business impact?
[07:30] Nina Park: Yes, each prompt and cluster can be given tags and estimated cost impact; we have an integration to map to revenue or SKU impact manually.
[07:42] Evan Liu: Are the per-prompt Deltas exportable as CSV?
[07:46] Diego Alvarez: Yep CSV/JSON export and API endpoints.
[08:00] [08:35] Tom Rivers: On data residency - your hosted region storage, can we pick EU-only storage?
[08:42] Nina Park: For Hosted we have region controls, EU-only retention and we can configure retention windows. For strict residency we recommend Private deployment with our VPC option.
[08:55] Priya Singh: Our legal team will want SOC2 and logs retention policy.
[09:00] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 and the audit log spec after the call.
[09:05] [09:25] Diego Alvarez: Back to A/B: here's the A/B chart with per-metric CIs. You can drill into subgroup performance by intent, user cohort, or prompt length. Also, we support reweighting of metrics for business goals (i.e., prioritize intent precision over fluency).
[09:55] Priya Singh: Can we set multiple metrics for alerts? Like intent-f1 drop OR latency spike?
[10:03] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely. Alert expressions can be boolean: (intent_f1 < 0.85 AND latency_p95 > 800ms) OR overall_qa < 0.9.
[10:20] [11:00] Evan Liu: How frequently do you evaluate? Nightly? Weekly?
[11:06] Diego Alvarez: Flexible. You can schedule daily/nightly or run on commit via CI integration. For heavy workloads we recommend nightly small-sample and weekly full runs.
[11:20] [12:00] Priya Singh: Regarding sample selection for A/B - can Redwood stratify by user segment, or do we need to pre-sample?
[12:06] Nina Park: We can stratify sampling on ingest fields, user cohorts, or you can provide custom sample lists as CSV.
[12:20] [13:00] Tom Rivers: What about false positives on alerts - we can't be paged for every tiny blip.
[13:10] Diego Alvarez: You can configure alert noise controls: cooldowns, multi-window checks, and require X consecutive windows or minimum effect size. Also mute rules per prompt-set.
[13:30] Priya Singh: Nice. Would like to see the historical trend visual with annotations when we roll a new prompt or model.
[13:38] Diego Alvarez: All available - annotate events, link to deploy IDs, and you can tie back to CI commits.
[13:50] [15:00] Maya Chen: Quick aside on cost: Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles per model and workload. We ran a suggestion that reduced token cost by ~35% for one customer while keeping QA delta < 1%.
[15:25] Evan Liu: Is quantization automatic? We want to test accuracy tradeoffs.
[15:29] Nina Park: It's recommendation first. We provide simulated evals and an expected quality delta estimate. You can run an A/B with quantized variant behind a canary.
[15:45] [17:00] Diego Alvarez: Showing API flow now - you POST prompt set, then call /evals/run with model variants list. Response gives progress ID, then results endpoint returns per-prompt metrics.
[17:30] Priya Singh: How big a prompt-set can we run? Millions?
[17:36] Diego Alvarez: We've handled multi-million prompt sets but for cost reasons we recommend sampling or sharding. For nightly full-run we recommend sharded jobs.
[17:55] [19:00] Evan Liu: For our integration we want webhook-based push to internal SQS. Is webhook auth supported?
[19:06] Diego Alvarez: Yes, HMAC-signed payloads, and you can deliver to internal endpoints via a customer VPN in the Private deployment.
[19:20] [20:00] Priya Singh: Can we do human-in-the-loop tagging for false negatives? Our team wants a simple curation UI.
[20:10] Nina Park: Yep built-in curation UI - you can flag, add notes, send to retrain queue, or export to your annotation tool.
[20:30] [21:00] *(brief cross-talk about specific prompt examples, a few words transcribed incorrectly: "KV cache" appears as "KV cash")*
[21:20] Diego Alvarez: I'm going to demo a regression-alert rule creation: set metric intent_f1, baseline pinned to last stable deploy, threshold absolute drop 4%, window 7 days, cooldown 24 hours.
[21:45] [22:10] Priya Singh: Can we escalate differently by severity? Low->Slack, High->PagerDuty?
[22:18] Diego Alvarez: Yep per-rule routing.
[22:30] [23:00] *(demo shows rule creation, user inputs, and test notification sent to a sample Slack channel)*
[23:30] Evan Liu: The test notification payload - can we include top 5 failing prompts in the message?
[23:36] Diego Alvarez: Yes, payload size is configurable and we can include attachments pointing to the Console for full context.
[23:50] [25:00] Priya Singh: About governance - RBAC for who can create rules vs who can acknowledge alerts?
[25:06] Nina Park: Full RBAC, audit logs for acknowledge/close, and SSO via SAML/SCIM.
[25:30] Tom Rivers: Good. Our security team will ask about key rotation and HSM support.
[25:36] Maya Chen: We'll include key rotation docs and HSM integration notes in the security pack.
[25:50] [27:00] Diego Alvarez: Next I'll show A/B drilldown: per-intent confusion matrices, token-level regressions, and a waterfall of suggested remediation: prompt rewrite, filtering, or model rollback.
[27:30] Priya Singh: Do you surface the exact tokens that cause hallucination?
[27:36] Diego Alvarez: We surface token-level attention proxies and compare top-k logits, it's noisy but helpful for triage.
[27:50] [29:00] Evan Liu: For our pilot, can we limit to two intents and 5k prompts?
[29:06] Maya Chen: Totally reasonable - that keeps cost manageable and gives signal. We'll provision eval environment for that.
[29:20] [30:00] Priya Singh: For A/B comparison, how do you handle sampling bias if one model responds faster so you get different truncation?
[30:08] Diego Alvarez: We control for generation params, enforce same decoding, and can simulate identical runtime truncation in evaluation. Differences are flagged in the report.
[30:40] [32:00] Tom Rivers: If we go Private later, will the evaluation pipelines port over?
[32:06] Nina Park: Yes, same Console and API semantics, just customer-managed infra and keys.
[32:20] [33:00] Priya Singh: Any limitations on embedding-based similarity for very short prompts?
[33:06] Diego Alvarez: Short prompts are tougher; we recommend augmenting with metadata and using ensemble metrics.
[33:40] [35:00] Maya Chen: OK let's do recap and next steps.
[35:05] Maya Chen: Action items - we'll send SOC2 and security pack (Maya), Diego will provision the eval account and drop sample prompts and API keys, Priya will share the priority prompt-sets and baseline metrics.
[35:30] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Also, we'd like a recommended default alert policy for retail ecomm use cases.
[35:38] Diego Alvarez: We'll include a retail recommend template - thresholds, cadence, and noise-filter settings.
[35:50] [36:30] Tom Rivers: We'll loop in Security and Legal once we have the docs.
[36:36] Evan Liu: Estimated time to integrate is ~2-3 days from getting API keys.
[36:42] Maya Chen: For pilot success criteria, propose: 1) run A/B across 5k prompts with measurable QA lift or stable model; 2) regression alerts configured and tested; 3) low false positive rate (<10%) on alerts during pilot. Agree?
[37:05] Priya Singh: Agree.
[37:10] [38:00] Maya Chen: Great. Final Qs?
[38:05] Priya Singh: One minor - can we export per-prompt human labels back into Redwood to retrain?
[38:12] Nina Park: Yes import/export supported via CSV/API.
[38:20] [40:00] *(wrap up, small talk about conference attendance, a mis-transcribed acronym "K8s" appears as "K-eight-s")*
[41:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll send the security pack and pricing, provision the eval env by Monday.
[41:15] Priya Singh: Thanks all.
[41:20] Tom Rivers: Thanks.
[41:25] Evan Liu: Thanks.
[47:30] *Call ends*

Notes: transcript contains minor ASR errors (proper nouns, acronyms). References to Redwood products: Console, Optimize, Eval; sometimes transcribed as Reedwood Opt or Redwood Opt.
